newsitem.title: DUBAI: U.S. to enforce Iraq no-fly zone at 0800 GMT.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to enforce Iraq no-fly zone at 0800 GMT.

text.p: United States warplanes will start enforcing an expanded no-fly zone in southern Iraq when it takes effect at 0800 GMT on Wednesday.

Lieutenant-Colonel Andy Bourland, U.S. Public Affairs Director for the Joint Task Force Southwest Asia, told Reuters warplanes involved in Operation Southern Watch "will enforce the no-fly zone as outlined by the President (Bill Clinton) on Tuesday".
He did not say what kind of aircraft would take part.
The United States has more than 300 warplanes deployed in and around the Gulf.

The U.S. decided on Tuesday to extend the air-exclusion zone in southern Iraq to the 33rd parallel, on the outskirts of Baghdad, from the 32nd parallel which was set up after Iraq's defeat in the 1991 Gulf War.

But Iraq has declared the original and wider zone in the south null and void. President Saddam Hussein also urged his pilots and anti-aircraft gunners to shoot down any Western plane entering that zone and another one in the north of the country.

The U.S. fired cruise missiles at Iraqi air defence targets in southern Iraq on Tuesday and Wednesday. The attacks were prompted by Saturday's incursion by Iraqi armed forces into Kurdish areas in northern Iraq.
Western military experts said the 44 cruise missile attacks were aimed at disabling key Iraqi installations in the south to facilitate the enforcement of a wider zone.
